name: j-aeneas-full
style: Adult male documentary narrator, warm and grounded, American English. Curious and quick on the opening question, clear and steady through the journey; place names and numbers a beat slower. When the father dies, slow down and soften, almost quiet. No hype, no shouting. The last line lands with quiet weight.

lines.text: Why did Aeneas, the hero Rome called its founder, wander for seven years, when Italy was three weeks' sail from Troy?
The answer is on this route, and in one goddess's grudge.
It begins in burning Troy, in modern Turkey.
Aeneas carries his old father out on his back.
First stop: Thrace, where a bleeding myrtle warns him to leave.
On Delos, Apollo's oracle tells him: seek your ancient mother.
His father reads it as Crete.
Then a plague drives them out.
In a dream, the gods correct him.
The mother is Italy, where his ancestors came from.
A storm throws them onto the islands of the Harpies.
Their curse: one day, you will be hungry enough to eat your tables.
At Buthrotum, a prophet warns him: don't take the short way.
Scylla and Charybdis guard the strait.
So they see Italy for the very first time, and have to sail on.
They circle Sicily, past the Cyclops under Mount Etna.
At Drepanum, his father dies.
The man he carried out of burning Troy never sees Italy.
Now the goddess strikes.
Juno loves one city above all, Carthage, and a prophecy says Aeneas' descendants will destroy it.
Her storm throws the fleet to Africa, right into Carthage.
Queen Dido tells him: this is your seventh summer at sea.
He stays, until the gods order him to leave.
Dido curses his people: our nations will be enemies forever.
That is how Virgil explains why Rome and Carthage later fought three wars.
At Cumae, the Sibyl leads him into the underworld, where his father shows him Rome.
At last, at the mouth of the Tiber, they use flat bread as plates, and eat them.
His son laughs: we're eating our tables.
The curse was a joke.
They had arrived.
Three weeks of sailing became seven years and more than three thousand kilometres.
A misread oracle, a strait he couldn't take, and a goddess who wanted him lost.
And his descendants, Romulus and Remus, would found Rome.
